discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and their quantized edge transport (quantum spin Hall and quantum anomalous Hall effects)

nominees.name: Qi-Kun Xue
nominees.affiliation: Southern University of Science and Technology and Tsinghua University, China

subfield: Condensed matter physics: topological phases and quantum transport
motivation: Kane (with the late E. J. Mele) showed that spin-orbit coupling can produce a new time-reversal-invariant electronic phase, classified by a Z2 invariant, with protected helical edge states, and extended it to three-dimensional topological insulators. Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental proof in 2007: quantized edge conductance in HgTe/CdTe quantum wells. They later confirmed nonlocal, helical edge transport. In 2013 Xue's group observed the quantum anomalous Hall effect in magnetically doped (Bi,Sb)2Te3 films: quantized Hall resistance at zero field, which earlier theory had linked to topological insulators. Together these works turned band topology from an abstraction into robust quantized transport in real, disordered materials. They founded a worldwide field spanning topological materials, Majorana platforms and dissipationless electronics, which has mobilised an entire generation of theorists and experimentalists.
